Fri

Jul 31Medium-low confidenceoutbound · 06:00–22:00 ET
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.NWS-hrNWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.NWS-dayNWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Extended outlook summary

.. (Today through Thursday) Issued at 546 AM EDT Wed Jul 29 2026 An overall less active pattern is expected through the short term. — .. (Thursday night through Tuesday) Issued at 546 AM EDT Wed Jul 29 2026 By Saturday, the next frontal boundary moves into western GA just before daybreak.

Short term

.. (Today through Thursday) Issued at 546 AM EDT Wed Jul 29 2026 An overall less active pattern is expected through the short term. For the afternoon, a heat advisory is in effect for the far southern portions of the CWA. That's also where we'll find the most likely chance to see afternoon thunderstorms as a boundary settles across central Georgia. The best chance for severe weather will likely be south of our CWA, but a few storms could contain damaging winds and frequent lightning. Generally less oppressive temperatures are expected this afternoon for most of the CWA, save for the far south where apparent temperatures are expected to rise into Heat Advisory territory. The rest of the CWA will see highs in the upper 80s and low 90s but with dewpoints in the 60s making it feel a lot more comfortable than what we've seen over the past few days. This trend will continue as we go into the second half of the work week, with pleasant temperatures and minimal chances of afternoon thunderstorms over the next 36 hours.

Long term

.. (Thursday night through Tuesday) Issued at 546 AM EDT Wed Jul 29 2026 By Saturday, the next frontal boundary moves into western GA just before daybreak. Models still indicate the system to be pretty well organized by the time it reaches the GA/AL border so it's something we'll need to keep an eye on the threat it poses over the next few days. The front stalls out and sets us up to return to a pattern of afternoon thunderstorms. With it being a source of lift through the weekend and into the start of next week, a few storms in the afternoon could become strong to severe. Temperatures through the rest of the long term should remain below heat advisory criteria, though the trend is for them to gradually increase through next week. Expect highs in the upper 80s and low 90s; regulated in part by at least some cooling during the afternoon.

Editorial #8 KTRI VFR Bristol/Tri-Cities Arpt, TN, US · Tri-Cities TN/VAETE1h11Dist168 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTRI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KTRI this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KROA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KROA this run.

Editorial #14 KSHD VFR Staunton/Shenandoah Valley Rgnl, VA, US · Shenandoah valleyETE2h25Dist355 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSHD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KCHO is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Editorial #3 KSSI VFR Brunswick/McKinnon St Simons Arpt, GA, US · St Simons beachETE1h29Dist214 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSSI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSSI this run.

Editorial #4 KJZI VFR Charleston Exec, SC, US · Charleston ExecETE1h28Dist213 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJZI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJZI this run.

Editorial #10 KSGJ MVFR St Augustine Arpt, FL, US · St Augustine FLETE1h55Dist276 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSGJ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSGJ this run.

A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KECP observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Editorial #17 KDAB VFR Daytona Beach Intl, FL, US · Daytona Beach (Class C)ETE2h13Dist324 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KDAB observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KDAB this run.

Editorial #21 KSPG VFR St Petersburg/Whitted Arpt, FL, US · St PetersburgETE2h35Dist379 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSPG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KPIE is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSPG this run.

Editorial #22 KTPF UNKNOWN — · Tampa Peter O KnightETE2h32Dist372 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. No usable current KTPF observation was available this run (state: unavailable). That says nothing about the forecast for this day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTPA is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KTPF this run.

Editorial #24 KVNC MVFR Venice Muni, FL, US · Venice FLETE2h51Dist422 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KVNC observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSRQ is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KVNC this run.

Editorial #19 KBFM VFR Mobile/Downtown Arpt, AL, US · Mobile DowntownETE2h00Dist290 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBFM observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KBFM this run.

Editorial #20 KGPT VFR Gulfport-Biloxi Intl, MS, US · Gulfport-BiloxiETE2h18Dist337 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGPT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KGPT this run.

METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHSA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KGPT is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHSA this run.

Editorial #27 KOPF VFR Miami/Opa Locka Arpt, FL, US · Miami-Opa LockaETE3h30Dist521 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KOPF this run.

Editorial #28 KHPN VFR White Plains/Westchester Cnty, NY, US · White Plains NYETE4h18Dist647 nm
METARMETAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.TAFTAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Jul 29 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.MAVGFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).MEXGFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).GFAGFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.NOTAMFAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHPN this run.

3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 16 SIGMET records, 22 G-AIRMET records, 2 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): Atlantic South: MVFR at KSGJ; Gulf East: MVFR at KVNC; Gulf East: category unavailable at KTPF; Long-range: MVFR at KBED.
Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • ☐ Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • ☐ Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • ☐ Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • ☐ NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • ☐ Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • ☐ Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • ☐ File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

★ Features

Available now

  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Four-day KLZU change-window board with four outbound/return planning alternatives
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the planned window — a day with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Download PDF — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS Pre-Production (sandbox) NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; active on this page with non-operational Pre-Production test data, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
